concepts.gloss_en: complete/perfect da'at — whole, mature knowledge (intellect in its state of completeness)

reason_for_human: All five occurrences express the same idea — da'at in its state of completeness (שלמות הדעת). The lm1:53 case is the nominal term 'דַּעַת הַשָּׁלֵם' (the complete da'at), while the four lm2:17 cases are the predicative 'הַדַּעַת שָׁלֵם' (the da'at is/is not complete) drawn from one paragraph; these differ only in definite-article placement and attributive-vs-predicative syntax, not in word or meaning, so they are one concept. Note the lm2:17 forms are really predicative sentences captured by the extractor, but they denote the identical archetype of complete da'at.
